drills.q: Service at 500 rps, 100ms avg latency, concurrency 80. Instances needed? Latency doubles - now what?
drills.a: in-flight = 500 x 0.1 = 50 -> 1 instance. At 200ms: 100 in flight -> 2 instances. Latency not rps drives the bill.

drills.q: p99 spikes to ~1.2s exactly once each morning. Diagnosis and two fixes with cost implications.
drills.a: Overnight scale-to-zero cold start on first request. Fix 1: min-instances=1 (continuous small cost). Fix 2: smaller image + lazy init + startup CPU boost (free-ish). Measure container/startup_latency first.

drills.q: Launch day traffic spike returns HTTP 429s. What happened and what do you check before raising max-instances?
drills.a: Hit max-instances (default 100/revision) with saturated queues and router timeouts. Before raising: downstream capacity - DB connection budget / per-instance pool size; NAT throughput; dependency rate limits. Cap is protection, not just cost knob.

drills.q: A metrics-scraper goroutine inside your service reports stale data intermittently. Root cause?
drills.a: Default CPU throttling freezes background threads between requests. Switch to always-allocated CPU (--no-cpu-throttling); accept continuous billing and pair with min-instances deliberately.

drills.q: Wire GCS uploads under gs://incoming/*.csv to a processor service. Which trigger type and why?
drills.a: Audit-log Eventarc trigger: type google.cloud.audit.log.v1.written, serviceName storage.googleapis.com, methodName storage.objects.create, resourceName path pattern /buckets/incoming/objects/*.csv. Direct object.v1.finalized events cannot prefix-filter.

drills.q: Processor runs twice for one upload occasionally. Why and what do you change?
drills.a: Pub/Sub-backed delivery is at-least-once (retries after slow/failed handling). Dedup on CloudEvent id or object name+generation in a fast store; keep handler fast or offload long work to jobs; monitor DLQ.

drills.q: Estimate monthly cost shape: steady 10 rps, 150ms, conc 80, 1 vCPU/512MB vs bursty 0-500 rps 5% of the time. Which pricing mode wins each?
drills.a: Steady: ~2 instances always -> instance-based/committed comparison vs small GKE pool; Cloud Run competitive but check GKE consolidation. Bursty: scale-to-zero request-based billing wins massively - pay only for the burst windows.

drills.q: Deploy must reach an internal 10.x API and present one fixed egress IP to a partner allowlist. Design.
drills.a: Direct VPC egress on a chosen subnet -> private routing; Cloud NAT on that subnet provides the static egress IP. Ingress: internal-and-cloud-load-balancing only.

drills.q: Interviewer says 'Cloud Functions can run 60 minutes.' Correct precisely.
drills.a: Cloud Run functions: HTTP-triggered up to 60 min; event-driven via Eventarc capped at 9 min; gen1 legacy capped at 9 min for everything. Longer than that = jobs/Batch/Workflows.

drills.q: Canary plan for a risky deploy using native features only.
drills.a: Deploy creates new revision; smoke-test revision URL; shift 5% traffic, watch per-revision error/latency metrics; promote 100% or roll back by retagging 100% to prior revision - seconds, no rebuild. Keep N-1 revisions warm if rollback speed matters.
